newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Pru to show steady progress in 1996.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Pru to show steady progress in 1996.

text.p: Prudential Corp, Britain's largest life insurance group, reports results on Wednesday with industry analysts expecting profits to show steady progress over the past year.
Just last month the Pru reported a strong rise in new business figures for 1996 and analysts' consensus profit forecasts of 851 million pounds for the year are six percent up on 1995.
At the half-way stage, the company beat analyst expectations with an eight percent rise in operating profits to 421 million pounds.
Those results included 33 million pounds in start up costs for the new tele-banking operation which began on October 1.

While the Pru said then that the life insurance business was benefiting from a general upturn in consumer confidence, single contribution products showed far more growth than those requiring a longer-term commitment or regular contributions.

The outlook for the life industry as a whole is generally accepted to be improving with changing demographics and the government backing away from state pension provision expected to drive demand going forward
The Pru's strategy remains to increase its customer base in the fragmented UK market, and develop its distribution channels and presence in retail banking.
Hopes for news next week on the company's negotiations with the Department of Trade & Industry (DTI) about ownership of so-called orphan assets are likely to be disappointed.

Earlier this week Britannic Assurance became the latest life insurer to agree a framework for distribution of these assets -- money built up in the with-profits funds which is surplus to policyholders' needs.
Analysts said it was unlikely the Pru would be forthcoming on the issue while negotiations with the DTI were continuing.
Two weeks ago it declined to comment on reports it was considering taking legal action against the DTI over delays in the process.
For the year as a whole Jackson National in the U.S. is expected to turn in a strong performance.
Product range has been diversified and profitability increased. One analyst is forecasting underlying profits growth for the unit of around 20 percent annually over the next three years.
The Pru's use of average exchange rates should mean the strength of sterling against the dollar well have a limited impact on the profits.

The market is likely to be looking for an indication of what the company intends to do with the 1.75 billion pounds it received from the sale of its Mercantile & General reinsurance business last August. Group chief executive Peter Davis said then that he was in no hurry to spend the money.
Only 250 million pounds of the company's 1.9 billion pound bid for mutually-owned Scottish Amicable is coming from shareholders funds.
At the half-year results, the company repeated its desire to buy a building society to expand its customer base but further news on that front has yet to emerge.
